text:
tim_customer: Hey team — we're seeing a bunch of JSON parse failures from the hosted API when using mode=json. ~10% of successful 200s come back with malformed JSON (truncated, trailing commas, or stray text). Started after yesterday's deploy. Sample raw response attached below. Also noticing occasional 401 spikes. Request id: req_3b9f2a. Any guidance?

alex_support: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact curl you used and the raw HTTP response (no pretty printing)? Are you using streaming? SDK version? Also confirm if you set a schema param.

Tim_customer: Using curl for repro: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood/ml/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXX' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"summarize...","mode":"json","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}}}}'`
Raw response (copied):
```
{"summary":"This is a short summary, with some details",}

Partial content: "more details coming...\n```

maria_engineer: Two common causes: 1) model output truncated (streaming or timeout) so you get a partial object; 2) model emits extra text or multiple JSON objects — client expects one. Short-term patterns that help: re-ask (ask the model to only output the JSON and nothing else), self-heal (send the malformed output back to the model with a repair prompt), and deterministic regex cleanup to fix trivial syntax issues (trailing commas, missing quotes).

alex_support: Also check if the 401s map to rotated keys, and whether any 402/billing errors happened around the same times. Billing interruptions sometimes cause unexpected responses.

chris_sre: If truncation is coming from streaming and the connection is closed early, try non-streaming or increase client timeout. We also have an `enforce_schema` flag in the SDK that will server-validate output and return a structured error instead of raw malformed JSON.

maria_engineer: Re-ask wrapper example (add this immediately after generation fails):
```text
If the output is not valid JSON, rewrite only the JSON so it is valid and conforms to the schema below. Output only the corrected JSON, nothing else.
Schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["summary"]}
```

maria_engineer: Heuristic regex cleanup (JS) — simple, not foolproof but reduces noise before trying an expensive model repair:
```js
// drop trailing commas in objects/arrays
body = body.replace(/,\s*(}|\])/g, '$1');
// wrap unquoted keys (basic)
body = body.replace(/([\{,]\s*)([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\s*:/g, '$1"$2":');
// remove stray leading/trailing non-json text
body = body.replace(/^[^\{\[]+/, '');
body = body.replace(/[^\}\]]+$/, '');
```
Use `JSON.parse` after these fixes; if parse still fails, fall back to a model repair step.

alex_support: Recommended retry/repair flow (cheap -> expensive):
1) Try to parse locally.
2) If parse fails, run deterministic regex sanitizer + parse.
3) If still fails, send a small repair prompt (re-ask) to the model asking it to return only valid JSON matching the schema.
4) If the repair fails, exponential backoff + re-generate. Example backoff: initial wait 200ms, multiply by 2 each try, add random jitter up to 100ms, cap at 2s. Limit total retries to 4.

alex_support: Also add correlation headers when you call the API: `X-Request-ID` and include `request_id` in the body where possible so we can find your logs.

chris_sre: If you can share a few failing `X-Request-ID`s we will tail ingress and worker logs. If malformed responses >5% for a customer we escalate to eng-runtime. For now, try the parse->regex->repair->backoff pattern.

alex_support: Quick curl repro harness to run against your env (please paste raw response + headers):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/ml/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: repro-123" \
  -d '{"input":"<prompt>","mode":"json","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"summary":{"type":"string"}}}}' -D -
```
Include the response headers and body so we can correlate.

maria_engineer: For customers hitting this frequently we've shipped a tiny client-side sanitizer (wasm/js) that runs the regex fixes + attempts a small token-limited repair via the model. I'll prepare a short gist.

alex_support: Action items: tim_customer -> run harness and paste raw output + any `X-Request-ID` values; maria_engineer -> share sanitizer gist; chris_sre -> check deploys for streaming timeout changes from yesterday. Marking P2 and will escalate to eng-runtime if we see >5% malformed rate. :manual_clock:

tim_customer: Thanks — will run and attach logs by EOD. Appreciate the triage!
